_about: Deployment configuration for plan-coder. Copy this file to deployment.local.json in the same directory and fill in your real values. deployment.local.json is gitignored and is the version actually used: bin/agent.py reads it at startup (credential-helper labels, transcript directory) and bin/render_prompts.py renders the prompt templates in prompts/ with it into local/ (also gitignored). Search order for the config: $PLAN_CODER_CONFIG, then config/deployment.local.json relative to the repo root, then ~/.plan-coder/deployment.json. Every field is optional; built-in defaults cover a standalone env-key setup. The optional plans section is the subscription-capacity model: each plan declares its id, vendor, API/CLI routes, tier-to-model map, and locked_to route allow-list (empty means unrestricted). Malformed plans are rejected on load; a providers-only config remains back-compatible as one API-only plan per provider. workers.max_tokens_out (0 = off) caps completion tokens per worker run and workers.cycle_tokens_out_budget (0 = off) caps completion tokens collected per supervisor cycle; both are pathological-burn guards, not quota limits — set them above the p99 of measured runs (see bin/trace_summary.py).

supervisor.quota_context: Quota is NOT the constraint; the human's merge bandwidth is. Mix quick wins and substantial issues as judgment dictates; small well-specified fixes merge fast.

goldfish._about: Goldfish brief-review spike (EGM pattern): zero-context cheap-tier review of triggered supervisor briefs before dispatch. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision. max_scope_files is the scope trigger threshold; goldfish tokens count inside the cycle budget.

jittest._about: JiTTest catching-test spike (hypothesis-first, Phase 0b shape): at PR collection, a triggered PR gets a balanced-tier hypothesis run (evidence-verified, per-changed-function coverage), one test run for the top hypothesis, a mechanical three-state gate and Stage A assessment; a surviving catch flags the PR jittest:catch for the operator. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision. Tokens count inside the cycle budget. max_three_state_runs is the test step's verify-loop budget; launch enforces the tokens-out caps as a hard stop.

exec_guard._about: Exec guard spike (Failproof-mined): Part A scrubs the worker shell environment (baseline + passthrough; provider env_keys and *KEY*/*TOKEN*/*SECRET*-shaped names stripped, strip set derived from providers config) and Part B denies a short scoped command list in Worker._exec (sudo, rm outside workdir/tmp/caches, .env reads, git push, mutating gh, curl|sh, find into harness state). Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision. scrub_always runs Part A while Part B stays off. passthrough names extra non-secret env vars workers may inherit; strip_extra names extra vars to strip.

edd._about: EDD spike Parts A+B (eval-driven development, Phase 0 PASS 2026-11-10; Part C killed in Phase 0 and is not built): harness fingerprint captured at dispatch into the receipt capture record, tune experiment ledger, per-case regression list for harness-tune. Deterministic, zero LLM tokens, never a merge/dispatch gate. Ships disabled; enabling (globally or per part) is a separate operator decision.

flagcheck._about: Flag-resolution verifier spike (Phase 0 PASS 2026-11-11; Phase 1 built 2026-11-11, ships disabled): bin/flagcheck.py deterministically re-verifies, per flagged PR, whether the condition behind the shepherd's needs-operator flag still holds — closed 8-class taxonomy (ci-none, ci-reds, ci-unclassified, workflow-kind, security-scan, conflict-stale, physics-gate, held-green), per-class states resolved_verified / unresolved / unverifiable with evidence and the timestamp it rests on. physics-gate is unverifiable until the operator's word is recorded in flag_resolutions.json (state dir; written only by the main agent from the operator's word). The ledger (flagcheck_ledger.jsonl) appends ONLY on first sight or state change. Visibility only: never clears a flag, never merges, never feeds the merge policy. exempt_checks below is the mapping the operator approved as data 2026-11-11 (fluxion: the ASHRAE Strict gate, the Fabric gate, the Scripts Test Suite and its gate wrapper, transcribed from the merge_policy prose); it changes only by an operator-approved edit. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision, after 2026-11-24.

flightdeck._about: Product-engineering spike Part C (Phase 0 PASS 2026-11-10, board audited 46/46 against live state): bin/flightdeck.py regenerates FLIGHT_DECK.md in the state dir from workers.json / shepherd.json / the ledgers at the end of each supervisor and shepherd cycle — Done / In progress / Next / Needs Alex / Spike windows (from an optional spike_windows.json registry in the state dir; absent registry is reported, never hardcoded). Deterministic, zero LLM tokens, generated never hand-edited, a view for the operator — never an input to a dispatch/merge/tune decision. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision.

claimcheck._about: Product-engineering spike Part D (Phase 0 PASS 2026-11-10, 48 claims re-typed, 2 premise-functioning unsupported found in SS-DFA): bin/claimcheck.py lints the ## Claims section of proposal artifacts (spike briefs, POC proposals/reports): every claim tagged [observed]/[inference]/[unsupported]/[decision], [observed] must cite a source, [unsupported] may never appear as a premise or in Verdict/Ask sections. Advisory only (exit 1 lists violations, blocks nothing); run by the artifact's author, no prompt wiring. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision.

worktree_persistence._about: Worktree persistence Phase 1 (plan-coder #87 Phase 0 / #89): at collection, a worker's worktree (with its in-tree build/dependency artifacts — target/, node_modules/, .venv/) is retained as a slot keyed by repo+issue instead of being removed, and a repeat dispatch of the same issue reuses that same path, reset with git clean -fdx -e target/ -e node_modules/ -e .venv/. Measured basis: same-path reuse 64s vs 707-899s cold cargo check (Phase 0) and 2.8-7.9s vs 571-596s first-cargo-step in the 2026-11-17 synthetic A/B; artifacts copied to a different path reuse nothing, so slots are never copied or shared across paths or issues. Ships disabled; enabling and per-repo opt-in are separate operator decisions. max_slots_per_repo caps retained slots per repo (closed-issue slots evict first, then least-recently-used).

edd._about: EDD (experiment-difference discipline) parts for the harness: 'fingerprint' captures the harness fingerprint at dispatch and logs one tune-pass experiment row per edit bundle (edd_experiments.jsonl), 'regress' compares worker-ledger windows around a fingerprint change. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision. EDD output is visibility only: never a merge gate, never a dispatch gate. A bundle row carries a per-bundle 'discriminator' so two edits to the SAME template in one pass stay separable.

verification_stamp._about: Verification stamp spike (issue #95, from #94 Part A): at supervisor collection, bin/verify_stamp.py classifies what a run actually verified (E2E/SUITE/TARGETED/NONE) from its transcript with the Phase 0 segment-anchored classifier and appends a stamp row (verify class, worker vs collection commands, clean_base_verified yes|no|not_claimed) to verification_ledger.jsonl in the state dir. OBSERVE-ONLY: nothing reads the stamp to gate, block, flag or grade anything. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision.

flagbatch._about: Batched flag view spike (feedback-surface flag review, Phase 1): bin/flagbatch.py renders a standalone FLAG_BATCH.md in the state dir at the end of each shepherd cycle — one deduplicated line per flagged PR, grouped by flag class (the flag-resolution verifier's class names), with repeat counts from the shepherd ledger, plus a counts-only flag_batch_ledger.jsonl for tune-pass reporting. Presentation only: never clears a flag, never a merge/dispatch/tune input. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision, after a 100% audit of the generated view against shepherd.json, the ledger, and live PR state.

shepherd.trigger_note: Adapt the trigger relay to your runner's mechanics.

test_tamper._about: Test-tamper flag check (issue #15): a mechanical scan of a PR diff that flags a worker PR modifying or deleting EXISTING test files without brief authorization (removed assertions, loosened tolerances, added skips/xfails). Flags only — it never merges, never blocks by force and never edits the PR; a flagged PR is left for the operator. New test files alone are never a flag, and a brief that authorized test changes is never a flag. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision.

judging_files._about: Judging-file flag (issue #96, from #94 Part C): a mechanical scan of a PR's changed files that flags a worker PR modifying or deleting a PRE-EXISTING judging file (gate/check script, lint config, CONTRACT.md) — visibility, not a tampering accusation. Routine ratchet/inventory touches are classified, never flagged; newly created gate files are classified creation, never flagged. Flags only — it never merges, never blocks by force and never edits the PR; a flagged PR is left for the operator. Ships disabled; enabling is a separate operator decision.
